A weak condenser fan motor run capacitor (rated 5 µF / 370 VAC) is swelling and losing capacitance, which reduces fan speed, raises head pressure on hot afternoons, and causes high-pressure lockouts [S2, S7]. 

**What to check and do:**
1. Isolate and lock out electrical power, verify zero voltage, and safely discharge components before touching anything [S2, S7].
2. Inspect the condenser coil for lint or obstructions, and inspect the condenser fan assembly and run capacitor for swelling, damage, or loose connections [S2, S7].
3. Test the isolated capacitor with a suitable instrument and replace it with the upgraded part number **VPN-0475** (5 µF / 440 VAC) if it is weak or damaged [S2, S7].
4. Update the board firmware via the USB-C port using the service app to fix overly sensitive momentary high-pressure trip counting (firmware 2.3 lacks debounce; update to version 2.4.1 or later) [S2].

The replacement part is compressor model VCP-150T, with a lead time of about three weeks, and you can keep the unit running temporarily on circuit 1 [S2].

1. **Verify circuit status**: Confirm circuit 1 is operating normally without active safety conditions and that circuit 2 has no electrical or mechanical problems affecting the first circuit [S2].

3. **Set control**: Disable circuit 2 using DIP switch 6 on the control board, following the VRL service instructions [S2].
4. **Communicate limits**: Inform the building manager that the unit will run on reduced capacity and may provide slower cooling under heavy load [S2].
